_about: The written disposition of every entry of
tests/fixtures/oracle_construct_reach_ledger.json that no SIBLING
reason-first ledger already decides. Reason-first: the reason is the
entry, the constructs are its evidence. Gated by
tools/oracle_construct_reach.py --check (roadmap item 533's second half).
An entry needs a line here only when no other file decides it. The
self-host byte-agreement ledger tests/fixtures/selfhost_blind_spots.json
(roadmap item 429) is reason-first too, per tier, over the SAME corpora:
emit_<tier> shares the tier's, and lower_ir's corpus IS the py tier's
(`_corpus_from_test("py")`). So a construct that appears under one of its
reasons is already disposed -- DERIVED, and recomputed from that file
rather than re-asserted here. What is left over is the two oracles no
tier covers: `compile` (IR sections, not emit.py constructs) and
`gate_census` (guarantee tags, not IR discriminants).
This file SHRINKS with the ledger it disposes of. A line whose construct
is no longer an unreached entry of the ledger fails --check and must be
DELETED, and a reason that is empty disposes of nothing. Never add a line
to silence a failure you have not read: the fix is a corpus document, or
a measured statement of why none can exist.
It records NAMES and prose only -- never counts, totals or line numbers.

compile.tests: UNPORTED, not a document owed. The `tests` IR section is populated only by in-file `test` bodies, and the native lowerer (selfhost/lower.rvl) has no arm that emits the section at all: the `"tests"` key appears in no IR assembly in that file, so the native chain drops a section the reference carries and NO document of this oracle's corpus can agree byte-for-byte on it. Adding one is a port of the section, not a corpus case.

gate_census.BOOT: REACHED OUT OF CORPUS. The census's own gate issues this tag for a program that is already in tests/test_selfhost_lower.py's in-memory tables (`REJECTED_PROGRAMS`, 'two boot components'), which _census_documents excludes by construction because they are strings, not documents; no corpus document elicits it. Pinned by tests/test_oracle_construct_reach.py::test_the_gate_census_unreached_tags_are_elicitable, which drives the census's gate over those tables and asserts this tag comes back.
